newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine wheat, maize prospects flourish in rain.
newsitem.headline: Argentine wheat, maize prospects flourish in rain.

text.p: Recent good rains have dispelled clowds of gloom from northern and central Argentine crop lands and regenerated prospects for wheat and maize, traders said Wednesday.
"I think we'll see 14 million-odd tonnes of wheat. I wouldn't have any fear predicting that," a trader told Reuters.
He said that rains in zones until now hardest hit by drought, in Cordoba province, will permit some farmers to dig up their shrivelled wheat and sow soybeans, maize or sunflower.

"They were scared to make the switch without rain, and risk ending up with two ruined crops," he said, "In other areas which were less badly hit the rain will let them stay with wheat, even though yields may be down 30 percent or 35 percent."
Traders said farmers were beginning maize sowing with enthusiasm in northern areas, and moisture levels have improved markedly everywhere except for a small area of southeastern Cordoba.
"My maize number is 12.5 million, 13 million tonnes. But it's still early, anything could happen," the first trader said.

"But the main thing is that it looks like the weather situation is getting back to normal," he said. He explained that he had heard a forecast for good rains up to November, a dry December, and then above average rain for the next few months.

Another trader agreed that the rains have greatly improved crop prospects: "We've avoided a disaster in wheat. Now to say we might get a crop of 14.5 million tonnes or 14.2 million tonnes is realistic again. Given normal rain from here on, the harvest is saved."

Maize, sunflower and soybean sowing prospects have also been improved, he said. "The soybean crop could easily be of similar size to last season. Although with more wheat planted there'll be a greater proportion of second crop beans, which yield less."
But he said that 10-12 percent less sunflower should be sown than last year, and that the dry spell has already foiled plans to sow sunflower in some 40,000 hectares in the north.

Argentine farmers produced some 9.2 million tonnes of wheat in 1995/96, along with 10.5 million tonnes of maize, 12.7 million tonnes of soybeans, and 5.6 million tonnes of sunflower seed, according to the Agricultural Secretariat.

The Secretariat said last week that wheat sowing has risen 35 percent from drought-blighted 1995/96. It expected maize sowing to rise by 5.7 percent, soybean sowing to fall by three percent, and sunflower sowing to dip 12.7 percent.
